US-119-HR10929.description: To impose a 50 percent rate of duty on hemp products imported from China and establish mandatory testing requirements for all imports of certain cannabinoid products, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10929.aiSummary: The bill would put a 50% import duty on certain hemp and cannabinoid products from China. It would also set new tariff categories for different kinds of cannabinoids and require testing of imported cannabinoid products for things like heavy metals, pesticides, germs, leftover solvents, and unknown compounds when they are meant for people to consume. The new duty would apply to covered imports entered 90 days after the bill becomes law, and federal agencies would publish yearly import and testing reports.

US-119-HR10907.description: To prohibit interference in elections for Federal office, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10907.aiSummary: The bill would add new civil remedies and longer time limits for certain election interference crimes tied to federal elections. It would also limit when law enforcement can seize ballots or election equipment and require chain-of-custody records if seizure happens. States could get grants to set up ballot tracking programs, with $50 million authorized for fiscal year 2027.

US-119-HR10808.description: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to allow additional contributions to a health savings account in the case of the birth or adoption of a child, and for other purposes.
US-119-HR10808.aiSummary: The bill would let people add an extra $2,000 to a health savings account when a child is born or adopted. It would apply for each qualifying child under age 18, and married couples could split the extra amount between them. The change would apply to tax years starting after December 31, 2026.

US-119-HR2306.title: Adams Memorial-Great American Heroes Act
US-119-HR2306.summary:
The Adams Memorial-Great American Heroes Act

This bill extends through 2032 the Adams Memorial Commission, whose purpose is to establish a permanent memorial in Washington, DC, to honor John Adams and his legacy.

The bill specifies that the Adams Memorial shall be located within the area specified by the Adams Memorial Commission in a February 25, 2025 map (i.e., south of the White House, adjacent to Ellipse Road and near Pennsylvania Avenue and 15th Street, Northwest).

If the Commission determines that this location is not suitable or feasible due to physical or security constraints, the bill requires that the memorial be located in the Reserve , an area which generally extends from the United States Capitol to the Lincoln Memorial, and from the White House to the Jefferson Memorial.

US-119-HR3978.title: Nuclear REFUEL (Recycling Efficient Fuels Utilizing Expedited Licensing) Act
US-119-HR3978.summary:
The following analysis is based on draft bill text that was made available by the House of Representatives and may differ from the bill text as introduced.

Nuclear REFUEL (Recycling Efficient Fuels Utilizing Expedited Licensing) Act

This bill directs the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) to license future recycling facilities that reprocess certain spent nuclear fuel (i.e., radioactive waste) under regulations for special nuclear material rather than regulations for production and utilization facilities. The bill applies to domestic facilities that reprocess spent nuclear fuel in a manner that does not isolate plutonium. Generally, such recycling facilities reprocess spent nuclear fuel into materials that may be reused as nuclear fuel for electricity.

While there are no commercial reprocessing facilities currently operating in the United States, the bill specifies which regulatory framework the NRC must use when issuing licenses to future facilities by excluding such facilities from the statutory definition of production facility . The licensing process under regulations for special nuclear material has fewer steps than the licensing process under regulations for production and utilization facilities.

US-119-HJRES131.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Bureau of Land Management relating to Coastal Plain Oil and Gas Leasing Program Record of Decision.
US-119-HJRES131.summary:
This joint resolution opens public land for oil and gas leasing in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge. Specifically, the joint resolution nullifies the record of decision (ROD) issued by the Bureau of Land Management on December 9, 2024, for the program that leases, develops, produces, and transports oil and gas in and from the Coastal Plain program area within the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge.

The 2024 ROD that is being nullified by this resolution replaced the 2020 ROD that made all of the approximately 1.6 million acres of the program area available for oil and gas leasing. The 2024 ROD made approximately 1.2 million acres unavailable for leasing or exploration in order to protect and conserve resources and certain uses in these areas. However, the 2024 ROD requires the statutory minimum of 400,000 acres to be made available for oil and gas leasing in a specified lease sale, subject to certain stipulations and operating procedures. Under current law, those acres must be located in the areas with the highest potential for the discovery of hydrocarbons.

US-119-HR1316.title: Maintaining American Superiority by Improving Export Control Transparency Act
US-119-HR1316.summary:
Maintaining American Superiority by Improving Export Control Transparency Act

This act requires the Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) to annually report to Congress on export control licensing.

Under current law, BIS administers and enforces controls on the export of dual-use goods (e.g., items with both civilian and military uses) and certain military parts and components. These export controls are implemented primarily under the Export Control Reform Act of 2018 (ECRA) through the Export Administration Regulations (EAR).

Under this act, BIS must annually report to Congress on license applications, other requests for authorization, and end-use checks (on-site verifications conducted by BIS) for the export, reexport, release, and in-country transfer of items subject to the EAR to covered entities. A covered entity is any entity that (1) is located in a country listed in Country Group D:5 (countries that are identified by the Department of State as subject to U.S. arms embargoes), and (2) is included on the Entity List or the Military End-User List (two of the lists published by BIS containing information on the individuals, organizations, and addresses subject to restrictions involving items subject to the EAR).

The act requires this report to include specified information, such as the name of the entity submitting the application, where the item is being exported, the decision with respect to the license application or authorization, and information on any end-use checks to ensure compliance with U.S. export controls. The information shall be exempt from public disclosure (except for aggregate statistics). Additionally, BIS must exclude from the report any information that could jeopardize an ongoing investigation.
